title: t19245: feat(pulse): wake external_trigger_pending holds when their named same-repo refs resolve
body:
## Summary

An external_trigger_pending hold now wakes on the first revisit pass after every same-repository #N its `Trigger awaited:` line names is a merged PR or an issue closed as completed. Before this, it waited for the fixed first-revisit interval (24h default, doubling to 7 days). In the anonymised private-repo sample, 4 of 38 holds were waiting up to a day on refs that had already resolved, and one was released by hand from an interactive session 4 minutes after its ref merged.

The bounded AI decision still judges the trigger. Only the wake-up is event-shaped:
- `_tbtr_trigger_refs` / `_tbtr_refs_resolved` / `_tbtr_refs_state` / `_tbtr_ref_wake_due`: extract up to 3 same-repo refs and fail closed. A read failure, an open ref or a closed-not-planned ref never wakes a hold early.
- Records persist `trigger_refs` and `refs_met`. A decision is bound to the ref state it saw, so a `still_pending` verdict on a compound trigger costs one AI call per resolution, not one per pass. A failed inference keeps the seen state, so resolved refs cannot bypass the 1h failure backoff.
- `_tbtr_order_refs`: waiting holds with unresolved named refs lead the pass, so a newly woken hold wins the per-pass AI budget (default 5).
- Legacy records without `trigger_refs` are read once to backfill them.

Unchanged: `trigger_met` posts the existing `terminal-blocker-circuit:retry` directive only with OWNER/MEMBER authority. Permission and source-access classes are never read. The dispatch negative cache keys on issue `updatedAt` (`pulse-dispatch-lib.sh:77-81`), so a wake-posted retry invalidates it without changing `next-due`.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-trigger-revisit.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — - `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`: Tests run: 64 failed: 0. New `_trigger_revisit_ref_wake_cases` cover each acceptance criterion: an unchanged hold with an open ref does only the ref read (no issue/comment reads, no AI); the first pass after the ref merges wakes it before the interval and records `refs_met: true`; a `still_pending` verdict with resolved refs is not re-asked on the next pass; a fresh hold on an already-resolved ref posts the retry at once; closed-not-planned refs never wake. Pass ordering asserts woken-candidate holds lead the AI budget.
- Read-only live check of the new helpers against real public GitHub refs: merged PR and completed issue resolve; open issue, not-planned issue and mixed merged+open do not; cross-repo `owner/other#5` is excluded from trigger refs; a resolution the record already saw does not wake; `ineligible` memos never wake. This confirms the REST `pull_request.merged_at` / `state_reason` shape the test stubs assume.
- `shellcheck -x` clean on both files; pre-commit ratchets pass.
- `complexity-regression-helper.sh check` for function-complexity and nesting-depth: no new violations. `_tbtr_issue` stays under 100 lines by extracting `_tbtr_decision_line` and `_tbtr_trigger_met`; the latter runs uncaptured so its `TRIGGER_REVISIT` log lines still reach stdout.
- The end-to-end pass (`terminal-blocker-trigger-revisit.sh run <owner/repo>` releasing resolved-ref holds with `decision=trigger_met`) is verified after deploy; the public repo has no live holds to exercise pre-merge.

Resolves #39670

title: t19247: fix(pulse): defer deploy reconciliation for supervising wrappers with a fresh LLM lock
body:
## Summary

Deploy reconciliation replaced every earlier-bundle Pulse PID past the 3600s drain ceiling unless it owned the instance lock with a fresh heartbeat. A supervising wrapper releases the instance lock before its LLM phase (t2774), so it never qualified and was SIGTERM/SIGKILLed mid-session. 2026-11-19 to 2026-11-21: 9 supervisor attempts, 4 completed, 5 lost; all 5 matched a forced reconciliation of the starting wrapper (ages 4106-6439s, all below the 7200s hard cap); 4 of 5 were blocker_recovery runs. Now a PID that owns LOCKDIR.llm with a pid file written within PULSE_LOCK_MAX_AGE (and no PID reuse) defers like a heartbeat lease, below the hard cap. Any deferred LLM-lock owner gets a drain marker in LOCKDIR.llm, and the wrapper skips its post-supervisor early-exit recycle fill when the marker names its PID, so the earlier bundle dispatches nothing new. Latent sibling path (_handle_stale_llm_lock judging by wrapper process age) filed as t19248 / GH#39683.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-sigpipe-llm-state.sh, TODO.md

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — Runtime probe on the production macOS host: sourced the PR-head pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh, spawned a live isolated pulse-wrapper.sh process, temp lock dirs, real ps/stat/launchd reads, drain ceiling 5s. Fresh LLM lock owned by the live PID: 'Pulse PID 95966 deferring: LLM supervisor lease fresh (age 7s, llm_lock 1s)', DEFER, LOCKDIR.llm/drain_requested = owner=95966 bundle=<active bundle>. LLM lock removed: 'without a fresh owner heartbeat lease or LLM supervisor lease; replacing it now', REPLACE. Suites: test-pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh 84 run 0 failed (new case: fresh/hard-cap/stale/future/foreign/missing/young); test-pulse-sigpipe-llm-state.sh PASS (drained supervisor skips recycle, foreign marker does not); test-pulse-wrapper-characterization, test-pulse-supervisor-starvation-escape, test-agent-deploy-pulse-runtime, test-pulse-lock-force-reclaim rc=0; shellcheck clean.

title: GH#39696: fix(routines): per-repo routine anchors for headless badge and workflow sync PRs (GH#39696)
body:
## Summary

Headless badge-sync and sync-workflows runs stamp origin:worker, but their PR bodies carried no explicit issue identity, so gh_create_pr rejected creation (GH#36877) and the t2449 gate never admitted pre-guard PRs that later runs skipped behind. routine-log-helper.sh gains ensure-anchor (one marker-located routine-tracking anchor issue per repo; a failed list fails closed) and ensure-pr-anchor (prepends Ref #N to an open origin:worker PR lacking identity via gh_pr_edit_safe). Both sync helpers resolve the anchor before pushing, write a standalone non-closing Ref #N, and backfill reused open PRs. routines.md documents the built-in anchors. No trust gate is weakened: the anchor provides identity only, and t2449 author/collaborator checks are unchanged.



## Files Changed

.agents/reference/routines.md, .agents/scripts/badges-sync-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/routine-log-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/sync-workflows-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-badges-sync-worktree.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-sync-workflows-helper.sh

## Decisions

Anchor located by a per-key HTML body marker under the routine-tracking label rather than local state, because these routines target many repos from one runner and must stay idempotent across machines. Lookup failure fails closed instead of creating, to avoid duplicate anchors. Backfill is limited to origin:worker PRs with no closing or explicit identity, so interactive or already-linked PRs are never rewritten.

## Runtime Testing

- **Verification:** self-assessed — shellcheck -x clean on all five changed scripts; pre-commit ratchets pass. bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-sync-workflows-helper.sh: 106 passed, including worker PR body identity and failed-anchor no-push/no-PR cases. bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-badges-sync-worktree.sh passed, including worker identity, failed-anchor no-push and reused-PR backfill. title: GH#39704: fix(claim-lifecycle): keep the interactive claim while another open PR still closes the issue (GH#39704)
body:
## Summary

planning-commit-helper.sh publishes an interactive task's TODO entry as a separate `For #N` planning PR that usually merges before the implementation PR. The t2811 permissive Ref/For fallback in release_interactive_claim_on_merge then released the implementing session's claim, unassigning the owner and flipping the issue to status:available while its implementation PR was still in review (observed today on GH#39696 at 16:08Z). Guard 4 now reads the issue's closedByPullRequestsReferences over GraphQL with each PR's state and keeps the claim, with a log line, when an OPEN closing PR other than the merged one remains. That projection also lists merged PRs, so state is checked explicitly. A failed lookup keeps the existing release so claims are never stranded. Both callers (pulse-merge post-merge actions and full-loop-helper merge) share this function.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/shared-claim-lifecycle.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge-auto-release.sh

## Decisions

Skip only on positive evidence of an OPEN closing PR; lookup failure preserves the release, because a stranded claim blocks dispatch until stale-claim recovery. The guard runs after the stamp guards, so it costs one GraphQL read only when a matching interactive claim exists. Direct GraphQL rather than gh issue view because the gh projection omits PR state and includes merged PRs.

title: GH#39710: fix(blocker-recovery): finish interrupted blocker releases and restore statusless AI-owned holds (GH#39710)

## Summary

set_issue_status writes remove-first (shared-gh-wrappers-status.sh:1165), so a blocker-recovery stage timeout (rc=124, 78 in pulse.log) or an interrupted dependency release between the remove and the add leaves an auto-dispatch issue with no status:* label and a blocked-owned companion: dispatch skips it and its owner no longer sees a hold. Field evidence on #39710: nine stranded issues in a managed repo (six needs-ai-recovery, three needs-dependency), reconciled by hand. Human holds, parent-task, needs-maintainer-review, non-task trackers and any status:* label are untouched. title: t19257: fix(pulse): ignore registry update stamps in the runner capability fingerprint
body:
## Summary

The runner capability fingerprint hashed the whole repos.json. aidevops update re-registers every repo, stamping updated/version on each entry, so every framework update (about 6 a day) looked like a capability change. Each runner_capability_unmet hold was discarded and a fresh worker rediscovered the same gap. In the local pulse log, two private-repo issues relaunched 9 and 8 times after a hold already existed, within about 25 minutes of each update. The fingerprint now hashes a jq projection of the registry without the per-entry updated/version stamps. Every other registry change (policy approval, pulse toggles, new repos) still wakes a re-probe as GH#35788 intended. An unparseable registry falls back to the raw-file checksum.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh

## Decisions

Kept every non-stamp registry change as a wake signal rather than narrowing to the repo's own entry, so the change stays minimal and conservative. Accepted a one-time re-probe per held issue after deployment because existing anchors carry the old raw-checksum format; no migration added.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — Sourced the changed lib against copies of the live 101-repo registry. Rewriting updated/version on every entry, deleting stamps, and compact reformatting leave the fingerprint unchanged. js_dependency_policy approval, a pulse toggle and a new repo entry change it. An invalid registry gives the deterministic raw-checksum fallback; an absent registry is stable. Suites: test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh 64/64 (includes the capability cooldown/anchor cases), test-dispatch-candidate-failure-reasons.sh pass, test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh 98/98, shellcheck -x clean. The projection costs 6.4 ms per call on the 53 KB registry. Fleet effect (no held-issue relaunch after an update) is observable only after deployment.

## Regression Evidence

Behaviour verified with an ad-hoc harness that sources pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh and exercises _dispatch_capability_config_fingerprint against copies of the live registry. Covered: stamp-only, semantic, new-repo, reformat, invalid and absent registry cases. Existing anchor suites still pass. No new test infrastructure added, per the time-to-functional policy.

Resolves #39723

Every scheduled routine run (session key `routine-<id>`, from `pulse-routines.sh` and `routine-helper.sh`) now starts in a fresh session. A legacy persisted row is cleared before launch, and no new row is stored after the run.

title: GH#39702: release drained aidevops-worker-* units after durable receipts
body:
## Summary

Adds worktree_lifetime_release.py, a bounded sweep run under the existing cleanup-worktrees-async lock. It releases (stop + reset-failed) aidevops-worker-* user units only when the current-boot invocation is drained (MainPID=0, no job, active/exited or failed/failed, unpopulated cgroup), every registry launch referencing it matches that invocation and boot, and the drained state has lasted past a 1h grace. The drained sample is committed to a new worktree_unit_releases SQLite receipt before the unit is resampled and stopped (systemd has no invocation-conditional StopUnit). drain_unit now accepts a matching same-boot receipt once the unit is not-found, so seal/proof/ready/resume keep working after release. Units with processes (live workers, MainPID=0 strays) are never stopped. Receipts from earlier boots are pruned.

Receipt storage, validation and the released-unit drain fallback live in the leaf module worktree_lifetime_release_receipt.py (lazily imported by drain_unit, following the existing worktree_lifetime_reconcile pattern) so the owner module does not grow past the Qlty file-complexity ratchet.

## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/cleanup-worktrees-async-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-systemd.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-owner-lifetime.py, .agents/scripts/worktree-managed-lifetime.py, .agents/scripts/worktree-managed-run.py, .agents/scripts/worktree_lifetime_owner.py, .agents/scripts/worktree_lifetime_release.py, .agents/scripts/worktree_lifetime_release_receipt.py

## Decisions

Option 2 per maintainer decision comment: release only after drained quiescence, never kill stray processes, no RuntimeMaxSec. Receipt-first ordering plus resample-before-stop narrows the non-atomic StopUnit window; lifetime rows are never rewritten. Unreferenced drained aidevops-worker units are also released (no registry evidence depends on them). Sweep is bounded (limit 200, 75s budget, 90s timeout) and failures retain units.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — runtime-verified: Docker debian systemd user manager (real systemd-run managed launches via worktree-managed-lifetime.py bind-exec): exited, failed and unreferenced units released; live worker and stray-descendant units retained; dry-run and default 1h grace change nothing; receiptless manual stop still makes seal refuse; ready/observe-idle/seal/proof succeed on released generations; resume attempt binds after a released predecessor; second sweep idempotent (24/24 PASS, re-run on the final refactored tree). title: GH#39746: feat: add VoiceStudio helper and MCP proxy for self-hosted TTS
body:
Resolves #39746

## What

This PR adds `voicestudio-helper.sh`, so any project can use a shared self-hosted [VoiceStudio](https://github.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio) speech server. It also adds a `voicestudio` on-demand MCP for agents.

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `.agents/scripts/voicestudio-helper.sh` | `status, voices, speak, transcribe, clone, mcp`. Injects `OMNIVOICE_API_KEY` via `aidevops secret NAME -- ...` (pattern: `netbird-mcp-launcher.sh`) |
| `.agents/scripts/voicestudio_client.py` | CLI commands (standard library only) |
| `.agents/scripts/voicestudio_api.py` | HTTP with an http(s)-only URL check. Splits text at paragraphs, sentences and clauses (default 220 chars, under the server's ~300 s GPU limit), retries 5xx answers with backoff, and joins WAV pieces |
| `.agents/scripts/voicestudio_mcp.py`, `voicestudio_mcp_files.py` | Stdio MCP proxy (transport, session re-initialisation) and its local-file request/result rewriting |
| `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/mcp-registry.mjs`, `agent-mcp-tools.mjs` | `voicestudio` local entry, `eager: false`, activation agent (pattern: `backblaze-b2`) |
| `.agents/tools/voice/voicestudio.md` | Agent doc |
| `reference/domain-index.md`, `tools/voice/voice-models.md`, `subagent-index.toon` | Routing rows |

Why a proxy instead of a `remote` entry or `mcp-remote`:
- Registry `remote` entries carry no auth header.
- VoiceStudio's `generate_speech` returns base64 WAV in both `content[].text` and `structuredContent`.

The proxy writes the WAV to `output_path` (or `VOICESTUDIO_OUTPUT_DIR`) and returns `audio_path`. It also uploads local files given as `audio_file` / `ref_audio_file`, so audio never enters the context.

## Verification

Live server (VoiceStudio 0.5.6, OmniVoice on CUDA):
- `speak --file` on two paragraphs with `--max-chars 70`: 3 pieces, 9.8 s MP3. `transcribe` of that MP3 returned the input text.
- MCP `initialize`, `tools/list` (local arguments advertised) and `generate_speech`: the reply went from ~150 KB to 576 bytes, with no base64, and the WAV was written to `output_path`.
- MCP `transcribe` with `audio_file`: transcript returned.
- `clone`: profile created, then deleted.
- One finding: a 5xx answer (CUDA OOM while other jobs held the shared GPU) was retried with backoff as designed.

Checks:
- `node --test` on `test-mcp-activation`, `test-on-demand-tools`, `test-v2-on-demand-mcp-agents` and `test-*-mcp-registry`: 58 pass, 0 fail, 7 skipped.

- `qlty smells` (including duplication): no smells. The four modules score 36, 23, 29 and 22 total complexity, after the first push hit `file-complexity` (114).
- Live checks above were re-run after the module split: same results.
- `extract-urls.py` against the allowlist: no unknown hosts.

No new tests were added: the generic activation tests already iterate every on-demand registry entry.

title: GH#39722: guarded stale Git lock repair and sanctioned canonical gc
body:
## Summary

Adds canonical-recovery-helper.sh repair-stale-locks and maintenance-gc (new canonical-recovery-hygiene.sh library). Both dry-run by default. Scope is the common Git dir only: refs/**.lock, logs/refs/**.lock, packed-refs.lock, the canonical index.lock, a gc.pid naming a dead local PID, and objects/pack tmp_*/.tmp-* temporaries. A candidate must be a regular file owned by the current user whose real parent stays inside the common dir, older than the threshold (60 min locks, 2 days pack temporaries), with no lsof/fuser holder and no live Git process for the repository that started before it was written; failed process or holder checks keep the file. --apply re-checks all gates under the canonical recovery lock, re-stats before rm, and writes one tamper-evident audit entry per file (relative path, size, mtime, hashed repo ID). maintenance-gc --apply then runs foreground git gc --auto and fails on 'failed to run reflog'. The canonical guard now points blocked git gc/maintenance/reflog/prune/repack/pack-refs at maintenance-gc. storage-cleanup-helper.sh gains a gitlocks store (r922 / aidevops cleanup) that runs repair-stale-locks for every registered canonical repo, applying only in apply mode. Docs: reference/dirty-worktree-preservation.md, reference/routines.md.

title: GH#39560: keep host Git policy shim off archive lifecycle helper PATH
body:
## Summary

Most of the remaining archive lifecycle suite wall time comes from the installed aidevops Git policy shim. When the shim leads PATH, as it does on normal interactive and worker hosts, every product Git call from the helpers also runs the shim's bash and Python guard. A shimmed call takes a median 242 ms against 30 ms native (~8x), measured at load 76-111 on a 16-core host. For the fixture's temporary repositories the shim's verdict is always "allowed", so this cost tests nothing.

`setUpClass` now builds a class-level helper PATH with `hermetic_helper_path` (in `worktree_archive_canonical_cases.py`). It puts a native-git symlink first only when the shim leads PATH. Any other leading `git` wrapper, such as `git-spawn-profile-helper.sh`, is kept, so spawn profiles still count every call. `guarded_object_import_proof` still installs the production shim explicitly.

Per maintainer direction that all work runs under load, the issue's acceptance criteria now use base/head runs started together on the same host instead of quiet-host absolute targets.

title: GH#39801: resolve omitted write target like native gh before the privacy guard
body:
## Summary

Root cause: every aidevops layer that must know where a GitHub write lands (privacy guard, REST fallback, PR recovery, labels, audit) read only an explicit --repo/-R, while native gh resolves an omitted target itself. So `gh-write-helper.sh pr create` without --repo reached privacy_guard_public_write with an empty slug and failed with the misleading 'target privacy could not be established' (GH#39801). Prior reports were point fixes of the same mismatch: GH#23883 (PR proof lost when gh_pr_list callers omitted --repo) and GH#30855 (-R not parsed).

Systemic fix: one shared resolver, `_gh_resolve_target_repo` in gh-closing-reference-lib.sh, mirrors native gh's non-interactive base-repo choice: -R/--repo, an issue/PR URL argument, GH_REPO, a `gh repo set-default` remote, then the github.com remote ranked upstream > github > origin. It makes no API calls and behaves the same in bash 3.2, bash 5 and zsh.
- Create, comment and edit wrappers (gh_create_issue, gh_create_pr, gh_issue_comment, gh_pr_comment, gh_issue_edit_safe, gh_pr_edit_safe) resolve the target once and pin it as --repo, so the guard, native transport, REST fallback and recovery act on the same repository. The create/comment prologue (stdin body, validation, target pin) is now one helper, `_gh_wrapper_prepare_write_args`, which also keeps gh_create_pr under the 100-line function limit.
- The gh shim privacy scan used origin only. It now uses the same resolver, which closes a real leak path: with a private origin and a public upstream, native gh writes to upstream, but the old scan checked origin, saw it was private and skipped the scan.
- Unresolvable, malformed or conflicting targets (URL vs --repo) block with a target-specific diagnostic before any visibility lookup. Unknown visibility still fails closed.



## Files Changed

.agents/reference/gh-command-discipline.md, .agents/scripts/gh, .agents/scripts/gh-closing-reference-lib.sh, .agents/scripts/privacy-guard-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-create.sh, .agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-safe-edit.sh, .agents/scripts/test-privacy-guard-shim.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-wrapper-public-deidentification.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-wrapper-repo-alias.sh, TODO.md

## Decisions

The target is pinned as --repo only when it came from GH_REPO or the checkout. URL targets stay as given because every stage already parses them. No API calls in the resolver; ssh host aliases and GHE hosts are not inferred and block with a clear 'pass --repo' diagnostic instead of guessing. Stale fixture fixed in test-gh-wrapper-public-deidentification.sh: worker PR bodies now need a For #N identity, and post-create provenance has separate coverage. Before this fix the allowlisted case failed on main and the 'blocks private person' case passed for the wrong reason. Follow-up #39814 (t19272): test-gh-wrapper-rest-fallback.sh reads live transport-admission state.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — Real CLI entrypoint A/B (`gh-write-helper.sh pr create --title ... --body-file ... --base main`, no --repo, run from a checkout, isolated HOME, recording gh transport): base commit fails with '[privacy-guard][BLOCK] Public-write target privacy could not be established.' and makes no gh call; this branch reaches native `pr create ... --repo up/public`. Shim A/B with the new upstream case: base 60/61 (the private-entity body goes through unscanned), branch 61/61. Native parity: resolver vs `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}` agree for origin+upstream (upstream) and for set-default origin (origin). Native cli/cli `pr create` source checked: --repo keeps git head detection. Tests passing: test-gh-wrapper-repo-alias (bash 3.2 and 5), test-gh-edit-safety (52/52), test-privacy-guard-shim, test-privacy-guard, test-gh-shim, test-gh-shim-native-resolution, test-gh-public-privacy-guard, test-gh-write-privacy-reporting, test-gh-wrapper-shell-compat (12/12), test-gh-write-batch-wrapper, test-pulse-merge-extract-linked-issue, test-gh-audit-anomaly-expected-transitions, test-origin-label-mutex-create (44/44), test-gh-wrapper-public-deidentification (6/6 after a stale-fixture fix), test-gh-wrapper-rest-fallback (all pass with isolated transport state; see #39814). ShellCheck clean; complexity-regression-helper check: 0 new violations.

Resolves #39801

title: t19273: fix(runner-capability): cache readable secret checks per pulse cycle
body:
## Summary

Parallel dispatch candidates and both admission gates re-decrypted the same secret names on every capability check (4708 runner_capability_check source=fresh lines, zero reuse). Under gpg-agent contention these hit check_timeout in bursts: 41 of 75 observed capability deferrals. runner-capability-helper.sh now records names that passed the secret readability check in the existing per-cycle state, under the existing exclusive cycle lock, and reuses them for AIDEVOPS_RUNNER_CAPABILITY_READABLE_TTL_SECONDS (default 300, clamped 0-1800, 0 disables). Only names and timestamps are stored, never values. Requirements parsing, rejections, missing names and timeouts stay uncached and are checked every time; any unreadable result clears the readable map. The secret-check loop and cache helpers moved into a new _runner_capability_python_secrets emitter so every emitter stays under the 100-line function gate (requirements emitter 100 -> 85 lines). Documented in reference/secret-handling.md.



## Files Changed

.agents/reference/secret-handling.md, .agents/scripts/runner-capability-helper.sh, TODO.md, todo/tasks/t19273-brief.md

## Decisions

Cache success only: a false positive at worst lets one launch reach the worker's own secret read, while caching failures could hide a fixed secret. Default TTL 300s bounds staleness after a secret is removed. Reused the existing cycle lock and state file rather than adding a new store. Extracted a secrets emitter instead of bypassing the complexity guard.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — Re-verified after the emitter extraction. title: t19275: fix: sync-workflows marker only for gate-admissible renders; keep anchors; refuse pin downgrade (GH#39830)
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #39828 (GH#39793). (1) One shared exact-render decision, `_routine_sync_render_admits` in `routine-pr-scope-lib.sh`, now serves both the merge gate (`_routine_sync_content`) and the publisher (`_sync_marker_eligible`). The publisher runs it over the exact bytes it will write and the caller at the PR merge base (default ref, or the fork point of an exact branch already checked out). A template rollout under a preserved older pin, an unreachable pin or any render mismatch therefore keeps the anchor identity instead of opening a marker PR the gate rejects. (2) The automatic `_sync_retire_anchor` after marker PRs is removed: anchor-path runs still need the anchor and `ensure-anchor` reuses only open anchors, so per-run retirement created a new anchor issue each alternating cycle. (3) The gate refuses a head pin older than the base caller's pin (`_routine_ref_not_older`: identical, or compare base...head = ahead). `routines.md` documents the parity and retained anchor.



## Files Changed

.agents/reference/routines.md, .agents/scripts/routine-pr-scope-lib.sh, .agents/scripts/sync-workflows-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-sync-workflows-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-briefed-trust-parity.sh, TODO.md

## Decisions

Publisher calls the gate's own function rather than re-implementing its checks, so parity holds by construction. Base caller comes from the merge-base commit, not the working tree, because that is what the gate compares. A base without a single 40-hex pin (e.g. floating @main) has no downgrade floor. body:
## Summary

commit-and-pr now refuses --testing-level runtime-pending when the derived runtime risk is Low or Medium, before any Git mutation. At those levels merge already accepts self-assessed evidence, so the hold-for-review only parked unfinished worker steps behind a human and stopped pulse redispatch. The refusal names the routes that keep work moving: push the branch and finish remaining steps before opening the PR, end with the brief's terminal blocker, or use self-assessed once completion criteria are met. Critical/High runtime-pending is unchanged. Updated the contract comment and the full-loop.md Runtime Testing Gate sentence.

.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-risk.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-runtime-risk.sh, .agents/workflows/full-loop.md

Deviation from the brief's route (a): it said to omit --ready so the PR opens as a draft. _gh_create_pr_should_default_draft (shared-gh-wrappers-create.sh) drafts only interactive-origin PRs, so a worker following that advice would open a non-draft, self-assessed PR that could merge and close the issue before its remaining steps ran. The refusal instead tells the runner to commit and git push -u origin HEAD without opening a PR, finish the steps on the branch, then run commit-and-pr with their evidence; this satisfies the observed repository guard (committed and pushed input) for every origin. title: GH#39837: fix(cloudron-release): make unsigned-request notice portable to macOS date and sed
body:
## Summary

release_notify_unsigned parsed the request created_at with GNU-only date -d, so on macOS (BSD date) the parse failed, the best-effort return swallowed it, and the GH#39788 unsigned-request notice never posted. It now tries GNU date -u -d, then TZ=UTC date -j -f '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' (the existing pattern in pulse-nmr-approval.sh). With the notice path reachable on macOS, a second GNU-only construct surfaced: release_not_routine_reason used a ';'-chained sed label script that BSD sed rejects ('undefined label'), leaving the notice's Why line empty. The script is now split into one -e per command, identical semantics on GNU and BSD sed.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh

## Decisions

The sed fix widens the issue's stated scope by one line in the same file and the same notice path; it was found while verifying the date fix and without it the macOS notice would post with an empty Why line.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — runtime-verified on macOS (BSD date/sed): bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-cloudron-release-approval.sh exits 0 and exercises the real release_notify_unsigned and release_not_routine_reason paths with fixtures; before the fix it failed at 'FAIL notice_old notices=0 expected=1' and printed sed 'undefined label'; after the fix notice_old, notice_posted, notice_young and unsigned all pass and the sed error is gone. shellcheck -x clean. affected-tests-helper.sh run --base origin/main: 7/7 selected suites pass (cloudron approval, merge guard, package init/monitor/routines, maintenance selector, pulse routines selector).

## Regression Evidence

The existing repository test .agents/scripts/tests/test-cloudron-release-approval.sh (cases notice_old/notice_posted) is already the regression test for this defect: on macOS with BSD date/sed it failed before this change ('FAIL notice_old notices=0 expected=1' plus sed 'undefined label') and passes after it. GitHub-hosted CI runs ubuntu with GNU date/sed, where the old code also worked, so no CI job can reproduce the BSD-only failure; a new test would add no signal beyond the existing case run on macOS. Manual evidence: local macOS run of that suite exits 0 after the fix.

Resolves #39837

title: t19281: fix(pulse): complete legacy Low/Medium runtime-pending holds
body:
## Summary

Route legacy Low/Medium runtime-pending worker PRs to an on-branch completion worker sharing the CI repair lease. Regenerate the original remote PR body through a guarded completion-only commit-and-pr path. Audit and lift only recorded runtime-pending-only holds after merge-ready evidence, preserving High/Critical interactive verification and ownership/PR-only boundaries.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh, .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-verify-runtime.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-feedback-ci-repair.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-runtime-pending-notice.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-verify-runtime.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-runtime-pending-notice.sh

## Decisions

Reuse the existing runtime body parser and CI repair lease rather than new parsing or orchestration. Independent review led to fresh prepublication ownership checks, dispatched-PR binding and an ancestry-proven exact-remote lease. No held PRs were visible in accessible live searches, so the requested real held Low/Medium example could not be obtained; controlled-path evidence is not presented as live-private-repository verification. Broader inherited failures reproduced on origin/main: default-branch-detection, agent-deploy-pulse-runtime, cloudron-release-approval, full-loop-completion-evidence, full-loop-merge-authority-guard, session-distill-provenance, worker-briefed-trust-parity, command-policy-helper, full-loop-merge-flag-conflict; later selection also reproduced full-loop-helper-coderabbit-reconcile (exit 127) on base. No unrelated repairs made.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — Runtime-exercised production routing, notice, hold-lift and original-branch publication functions with controlled GitHub/Git fixtures: verify-runtime suite 71 checks passed, runtime-pending notice/dispatcher/prompt suite passed. Affected suites: initial 30/30 pass; broader 80 suites had 71 passes and 9 base-reproduced failures; later 30-suite selection had 28 passes and 2 base-reproduced failures, no regressions. Bash syntax, diff checks and commit hooks passed. ShellCheck binary unavailable behind its wrapper; CI ShellCheck covers changed scripts. TypeScript dependencies absent; pre-push defers typecheck to CI.

Resolves #39849 (t19281).

- Extend runtime-pending notice JSON with the existing parser's risk and verification level
- Route legacy Low/Medium held PRs through an on-branch completion worker, sharing the CI repair lease to prevent overlapping writers
- Lift only recorded runtime-pending-only holds after a merge-ready Low/Medium body, with audit evidence and fresh head/scope checks
- Preserve High/Critical interactive verification and external/no-takeover/PR-only boundaries

## Verification

Implementation checkpoint; verification and readiness review in progress.
Affected tests: 30/30 selected suites passed, including runtime pending notice, verify-runtime and CI repair routing.
